# Sandaka Sutta (MN 76 (PTS MN i 513))

**ID:** MN 76 (PTS MN i 513)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Sandaka Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** With Sandaka
**PTS:** MN i 513
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0202m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The sutta satirizes claims of omniscience by describing a teacher who gets no alms, takes a wrong path, or must ask the name of a village, offering evasive rationalizations when events contradict his claim [Anālayo, Dawn of Abhidharma; McClintock 2010]. Sandaka is so persuaded by Ānanda's exposition that he urges his community to take up the Buddha's dispensation [Freedman 1977].

Parallels to the text are found in Sanskrit fragments (SF 294, SHT sutta 27), which expand the satire of the omniscient teacher to falling into a ditch or banging his head against a door [Anālayo, Dawn of Abhidharma]. The text shares extensive doctrinal formulas with other discourses in the Pali Canon, most notably the *Sāmaññaphala Sutta* (DN 2) and *Apaṇṇaka Sutta* (MN 60), which DharmaNexus corroborates with major textual overlaps [DharmaNexus; Freedman 1977].
